statement:
# Foundations of candidate higher prisms

Problem identifier: `higher_prisms/foundations`.

Researcher: Xiansheng Li. Prepared 2026-10-08.

## Authorized research objective

Establish a rigorous foundational theory for the candidate pair stated below. Audit its mathematical meaning, prove the foundational properties that hold, and give precise counterexamples to claims that fail. This is a research and proof-verification task using the existing Rethlas workflow. The object under investigation is the candidate higher prism itself.

The current assignment is the foundations part only. Arithmetic and topological applications will be a subsequent project. No relationship between the unindexed prism ideal $J$ and any indexed geometric Witt ideals $J_d$ is proposed or requested. Historical reference files may mention such a relationship; those passages are outside this assignment.

Preserve the user's existing runner, model, reasoning, search, and iteration settings. This packet supplies no iteration, time, or token limit. Use the ordinary proof-generation and whole-proof verification workflow. Do not substitute a candidate-discovery report for the foundational proofs.

The candidate and the sketches supplied here are research inputs, not accepted theorems. If a claim is false, prove an appropriately scoped negative result, identify the failure mechanism, and distinguish any repaired definition from the original. Do not silently add hypotheses, change the field points or lifts, replace integral operations by additive operations, or certify a conditional construction as an unconditional result.

## Mathematical setting and original candidate

Fix a prime $p$, a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a one-dimensional formal group of finite height $h$ over $k$, and its Lubin–Tate theory $E$. Put
\[
O=\pi_0 E\simeq W(k)[[u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1}]],\qquad
\mathfrak m=(p,u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1}).
\]
Use the actual integral Rezk power-operation theory $\mathbb T_E$ and its cofree Witt functor $\mathbb W_E$. State precisely which grading, algebra category, and completion are meant.

The proposed classical candidate is a pair $(A,J)$ with:

1. $A$ a full integral $\mathbb T_E$-algebra in a category compatible with the cofree Witt functor.
2. $J\subset A$ locally generated by a regular sequence of length $h$.
3. $A$ derived $(\mathfrak m A+J)$-complete.
4. For every perfect field extension $K/k$ and every compatible $O$-algebra map $f:A/J\to K$, with $O$ acting on $K$ through $k$, let $\widetilde f:A\to O_K=\mathbb W_E(K)$ be the canonical operation-compatible cofree lift of the composite $A\to A/J\to K$. Require the canonical map
\[
O_K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/J\longrightarrow K
\]
to be an equivalence.

The anticipated coefficient identification is
\[
O_K\simeq W(K)[[u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1}]],\qquad
\mathfrak m_K=(p,u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1}).
\]
Its meaning and naturality, including the tensor product and completion conventions, must be justified. The lift is not an arbitrary ring lift.

The immutable repository snapshot in the reference bundle records the original proposal. This packet makes its setting self-contained and specifies the current scope.

## Required foundation A: categories, lifts, and field detection

Specify an actual ambient integral operation-algebra category in which the candidate is meaningful. Give the precise cofree mapping property producing $\widetilde f$, prove that its reduction is the given field point, and justify the coefficient identification. Explain how the ordinary category and any completed or animated categories used are related. Keep the module monad, the theory over commutative algebras, and the additive operation algebra distinct.

Identify the topology on $A$, $A/J$, and $O_K$, and whether a field point or a lift must be continuous. Prove any automatic continuity used. Do not replace joint $(\mathfrak m A+J)$-completeness by a different completeness condition without an argument.

Establish the range in which the specified perfect fields detect the relevant local conditions. In particular, justify using perfected residue fields and the Jacobson-radical arguments needed later; address nonvacuity for nonzero complete objects. Separate noetherian arguments from statements valid for arbitrary rings.

Coordinate choices should be used for computation only. State the intrinsic coefficient object and how changes of coordinates or the underlying marked formal-group data transport the definition.

## Required foundation B: local primitivity and its intrinsic meaning

Prove or correct the proposed equivalence between fieldwise normalization and invertibility of
\[
(J/J^2)\otimes_{A/J,f}K\longrightarrow
\mathfrak m_K/\mathfrak m_K^2.
\]
For local regular generators $d_1,\ldots,d_h$, explicitly construct this map and show its independence from generators and coordinate trivializations.

Audit the Koszul argument: write $q_i=\widetilde f(d_i)$, identify the derived base change with the Koszul complex on the $q_i$, and compare its equivalence to $K$, generation of $\mathfrak m_K$, and the conormal basis condition. Justify localization at a field point even if the initial regular generators exist only locally.

Separate the role of regularity of the immersion from local freeness of its conormal module. Record the assumptions actually needed and exhibit failures of stronger formulations when they occur.

An intrinsic formulation of the conormal map is required. Investigate whether integral power operations give a more explicit criterion analogous to distinguishedness. Prove any such criterion claimed, including its scope. A general finite-operation formula is not presumed to exist; keep any unresolved strengthening distinct from the proved conormal theorem.

## Required foundation C: exact height-one recovery

At $h=1$, establish the comparison with ordinary prisms under explicit coefficient and completeness conventions. Use the actual height-one integral theory and compare it to $\delta$-rings. Specify whether the statement concerns prisms with a chosen compatible $W(k)$-structure, and distinguish orientable and locally principal ideals.

Check both directions of the equivalence with the classical prism condition. In a local generator calculation with $\widetilde f(d)=pu$, keep track of the distinction between the conormal scalar $\bar u$ and
\[
f(\delta(d))=\bar u^{\,p}.
\]
Use the actual hypotheses of Bhatt–Lurie and Bhatt–Scholze, including the local/global and Jacobson-radical steps. Do not import boundedness unless it is required for the statement being made.

## Required foundation D: examples and falsification

Resolve the following tests with the actual integral operations.

- Normalization: $(O,\mathfrak m)$.
- Nonprimitive regular sequence: $(O,(p^2,u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1}))$.
- The ramified family
\[
A=E^0(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})\simeq O[[x]],\qquad
J=(F(x),u_1-f_1(x),\ldots,u_{h-1}-f_{h-1}(x)),
\]
where $F(x)\in W(k)[x]$ is Eisenstein and $f_i(x)\in xW(k)[[x]]$.
- The height-two specialization $J=(x^e-p,u-x)$ for $e\ge2$.

For the ramified family, justify the full operation structure and augmentation, the regular sequence, the completeness, the quotient description, the perfect-field points, and the identity of the canonical lift. Check the claimed image sequence $(F(0),u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1})$ using cofreeness. The appearance of an Eisenstein polynomial alone does not identify the operations with a familiar Breuil–Kisin $\delta$-structure.

Develop further examples and counterexamples adaptively to test torsion, singularity, failure of regularity, nonflat base change, and the selected completeness hypotheses. A proper prism ideal is not required to be stable under all power operations; $A/J$ is not automatically an operation algebra.

## Required foundation E: morphisms and rigidity

Define morphisms using operation-compatible $O$-algebra maps $g:A\to B$ satisfying $g(J)\subseteq L$, together with any topology requirements established above.

Audit the proposed rigidity theorem: for suitable candidate pairs $(A,J)$ and $(B,L)$, does such a map force
\[
JB=L,\qquad B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/J\simeq B/L?
\]
First resolve a precisely stated noetherian complete version, then identify and prove the extent of generality supported by the argument. Check compatibility of canonical cofree lifts, the conormal comparison at perfected residue fields, Nakayama, and the regularity of the image sequence. An equality of ordinary ideals alone does not prove the derived assertion.

If a proposed extension of rigidity fails, supply a fully checked counterexample or identify the exact missing hypothesis. Distinguish the category of candidate pairs from the category of operation algebras over one fixed pair.

## Required foundation F: base change and descent

Prove a useful base-change theorem in an explicitly specified class, beginning with operation-compatible flat maps satisfying the appropriate completeness conditions. Address the completion operation itself, including preservation of the operation structure and regularity where used. Do not assert arbitrary base change of ordinary regular sequences.

Specify a class of covers for which pairs and their morphisms descend, and prove effective descent in that class. Suitable starting cases are faithfully flat finite locally free maps between complete operation algebras and appropriately formulated formal Zariski covers. State precisely which operation structure and compatible descent datum are part of the input; prove descent of the ideal, its regular immersion property, and the fieldwise normalization. Check how perfect residue-field extensions and their canonical lifts enter the descent argument.

The final theorem must identify the covers for which descent is actually established. A descent theorem for ordinary rings, modules, or coefficient correspondences alone is not a descent theorem for these pairs.

## Derived scope and further foundations

Determine which classical statements above require noetherian or torsion assumptions. Explore whether replacing the regular quotient by a derived regular immersion of codimension $h$ supplies a base-change-stable formulation, and give a precise proposed category and comparison with the classical pairs.

The required final account must explain the status of this extension. Prove every derived assertion included in the main theorem. Questions about a general animated or unbounded extension may remain explicitly identified as further work after the classical package has been fully resolved. A full envelope, cohomology theory, Nygaard filtration, or arithmetic/topological application is not an obligation of this foundations task.

## Evidence, references, and verification

Read the reference guide first. The supplied repository notes and assistant sketches are unverified research inputs. Historical claims, including any file named “verified” in prior projects, do not certify this candidate. Primary-source texts may have imperfect extraction; check the original source when notation or theorem hypotheses are unclear.

Preserve definitions, hypotheses, failures, counterexamples, and proof dependencies in the existing append-only Rethlas memory. Use the existing search and verification tools according to the generation workflow. Where independent reasoning yields a proof, write it in full; where a source is used, include its precise applicable statement and identifiers.

Maintain a claim-status table for foundations A–F. Each resolved claim must point to a proof or a counterexample with exact scope. Unresolved required claims keep the full package incomplete. A negative resolution is valid mathematics, but a failure to find a proof is not a counterexample.

Assemble the whole foundational argument before submitting it to the proof verifier. Keep a working `blueprint.md`; publish `blueprint_verified.md` only through the existing successful verification workflow. Preserve the exact submission, verifier report, and provenance. Supply a concise research summary and dependency/claim table with the completed package. Do not compile LaTeX.

## Complete target statement

For the candidate higher-prism pair $(A,J)$ defined in this problem, establish a mathematically explicit integral ambient category and canonical perfect-field lifts, and resolve foundations A–F by complete proofs or precise proved counterexamples. The resulting foundational theorem must state the exact hypotheses under which the conormal characterization, height-one recovery, normalization and ramified examples, morphism rigidity, base change, and effective descent hold. It must distinguish the original candidate from any repaired variant, identify the scope of nonnoetherian and derived extensions, and separate further questions from the verified classical results. The final proof must not presume a relationship with indexed Witt ideals or a pre-existing higher prismatic cohomology theory.

verification_report.summary: The complete proof passes sequential verification within its stated scopes. A–B establish the full integral category, canonical field lifts, completed coefficient identification, topology, field detection and intrinsic conormal criterion, using the applicable [Rezk inputs](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.12490v1). C correctly recovers all classical prisms with compatible W(k)-structure, without boundedness, and distinguishes the conormal scalar from its pth power; the comparison agrees with [Bhatt–Scholze](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4) and [Bhatt–Lurie](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.06124v1). D verifies the specified examples and the integral torsion, regularity and completeness counterexamples. E proves both ideal equality and derived rigidity for arbitrary classical candidates. F proves flat base change with target joint completeness, full operation extension to noetherian joint completions, and effective descent of noetherian pairs along faithfully flat finite locally free operation-algebra covers with compatible descent data. G proves the separate discrete-base derived extension and its explicitly scoped classical comparison. General animated bases, unrestricted nonnoetherian completion and formal Zariski descent remain outside the asserted results. All cited inputs were checked for matching definitions and hypotheses. No critical errors or gaps were found.
